4 اعناهُ He rendered him lowly, humble, or submissive. (S, TA.) ―
-b2- And (TA) He made him (Msb, K, TA) to stick fast in captivity, (Msb,) or to be, (K,) or to remain, or continue, (TA,) a captive. (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 1, in two places. ―
-b2- [Hence,] اعني الوَلِىُّ الأَرْضَ The وَلِىّ, i. e. the rain after the وَسْمِىّ, watered the land so that it gave growth to plants, or herbage. (S, * IKtt, TA.) ―
-b3- And اعنى الرَّجُلُ The man found, or lighted on, land that had produced herbage such as is termed عُشْب, [for قد اعشرت (to which I cannot assign any apposite meaning) in my original, I read قَدْ أَعْشَبَتْ], and of which the pasturage had become abundant. (TA.) ＝
-A3- See also Q. Q. 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
